newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures cut losses late, end mixed.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures cut losses late, end mixed.

text.p: IMM currency futures cut losses during a late move back up and ended pit trading barely mixed.

During the final hour, most futures ambled back up from day's lows in spotty trading as players, nervous about the possibility of central bank intervention, apparently covered shorts in spite of a further rise in U.S. stocks and bonds.
"Every night there are stories about intervention," said one currency floor broker after the close. "It seems to me its (rise)...squaring up."
Futures had eroded steadily into midday, as U.S. Treasury bonds rose and Dow 30 index cleared 7000 for the first time.
Floor traders instead focused on the prospects for intervention after rumors circulated Thursday that the Bank of England had covertly bought yen for dollars.
They also said the BoE and Federal Reserve were rumored to have checked rates to buy marks against the U.S. unit.

Still, traders said dollar buyers were likely to persist until the central banks actually show their hands, and even then any dollar selling was expected merely to brake rather tha reverse the dollar's rise.
"They're (traders) going to keep pounding it until they (central banks) come in," said the floor broker.

"I think a lot of it (intervention) would be given back right away," said another broker, noting that many players mentally already have considered their options if the central banks were to enter during holiday-thinned markets this long U.S. holiday weekend.
"Its (intervention) already happened in ours minds 20 times," he added. "When they do intervene, we have all our bases covered."
Pit trading in IMM currency futures closes early Friday at 1200 CST/1800 GMT and will stay shut Monday, February 17, for U.S. President's Day.
The morning's pullback shoved March Swiss francs to a new contract low, while nearby marks and yen each flirted with their contract lows.
Currencies had scant response to lower-than-expected U.S. retail sales data and an unexpectd drop in jobless claims.
Friday's January U.S. producer price index is seen rising 0.3 percent and gaining 0.2 percent in the core rate.

March yen fell $0.000024 at $0.008068, mark rose $0.0002 to $0.5950, Swiss franc fell $0.0029 to $0.6894, sterling fell $0.0092 to $1.6232, Can dollar rose $0.0028 to $0.7415, Mex peso rose $0.000125 to $0.126700. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
